atoms.text: This guide configures access for Tallymill, a batch query service that reads Parquet files from an input prefix and writes result sets to an output prefix. The bucket analytics-warehouse-prod and the IAM role TallymillQueryRole both belong to account 111122223333. Access is granted entirely through the role's identity-based policy. Attach a policy to TallymillQueryRole that allows storage:ListBucket on the bucket, restricted to the prefix inputs/. Add storage:GetObject on analytics-warehouse-prod/inputs/* so the service can read source files. Add storage:PutObject on analytics-warehouse-prod/results/* so query output can be written. Do not modify the bucket policy, because same-account access does not require a bucket policy statement. Run a test query and confirm that result files appear under results/ with the role as the writer.

This guide configures access for Tallymill, a batch query service that reads Parquet files from an input prefix and writes result sets to an output prefix. The bucket analytics-warehouse-prod belongs to account 444455556666, while the IAM role TallymillQueryRole belongs to account 111122223333. Access crosses the account boundary and is granted by the bucket owner through a bucket policy. In account 444455556666, add a statement whose principal is arn:iam::111122223333:role/TallymillQueryRole. Allow storage:ListBucket on the bucket, with a condition limiting listing to the prefix inputs/. Allow storage:GetObject on analytics-warehouse-prod/inputs/* and storage:PutObject on analytics-warehouse-prod/results/*. The administrator of account 111122223333 must also permit these same actions in the role's own policy. Run a test query and confirm that result files appear under results/ with the role as the writer.

This guide sets up access for Rivulet, a log ingestion service that reads raw gzip log files and writes compacted hourly partitions. The bucket edge-logs-landing and the IAM role RivuletCompactorRole are both in account 555500001111. The grant is carried only by the role's identity-based policy. Attach a policy to RivuletCompactorRole that allows storage:ListBucket on edge-logs-landing for the prefix raw/. Allow storage:GetObject and storage:DeleteObject on edge-logs-landing/raw/* so processed inputs can be removed after compaction. Allow storage:PutObject on edge-logs-landing/compacted/* for the partitioned output. Leave the bucket policy unchanged, since no cross-account statement is needed. After a compaction cycle, verify that files named by hour appear under compacted/ and that processed raw files are gone.

This guide sets up access for Rivulet, a log ingestion service that reads raw gzip log files and writes compacted hourly partitions. The bucket edge-logs-landing is owned by account 777788889999, and the IAM role RivuletCompactorRole is in account 555500001111. The grant is carried by a bucket policy that the bucket owner adds. In account 777788889999, add a statement naming account 555500001111 as the principal. Allow storage:ListBucket on edge-logs-landing for the prefix raw/. Allow storage:GetObject and storage:DeleteObject on edge-logs-landing/raw/* so processed inputs can be removed after compaction. Allow storage:PutObject on edge-logs-landing/compacted/* for the partitioned output. The administrator of account 555500001111 must delegate these actions to RivuletCompactorRole in its policy. After a compaction cycle, verify that files named by hour appear under compacted/ and that processed raw files are gone.

This guide covers access for Cleanflow, an ETL runner that reads CSV drops from a vendor-delivery prefix and writes validated datasets and rejected-row files. The bucket partner-intake-data and the IAM role CleanflowJobRole are in the same account, 222233334444. Permissions come only from the role's identity-based policy. Allow storage:ListBucket on partner-intake-data with a prefix condition of deliveries/. Allow storage:GetObject on partner-intake-data/deliveries/*. Allow storage:PutObject on partner-intake-data/validated/* and partner-intake-data/rejected/*. Do not edit the bucket policy. Submit a sample CSV, then confirm that a validated file and a rejected-rows file are both created with the expected row counts.

This guide covers access for Cleanflow, an ETL runner that reads CSV drops from a vendor-delivery prefix and writes validated datasets and rejected-row files. The bucket partner-intake-data is owned by account 666677778888, and the IAM role CleanflowJobRole is in account 222233334444. The bucket owner grants access with a bucket policy statement. Add a statement in account 666677778888 whose principal is arn:iam::222233334444:role/CleanflowJobRole. Allow storage:ListBucket on partner-intake-data with a prefix condition of deliveries/. Allow storage:GetObject on partner-intake-data/deliveries/*, and storage:PutObject on partner-intake-data/validated/* and partner-intake-data/rejected/*. The role's own account must also allow these actions in the role's policy. Submit a sample CSV, then confirm that a validated file and a rejected-rows file are both created with the expected row counts.

This guide configures a scheduled report generator, Ledgerline, which reads daily event tables and writes PDF and CSV report exports. The bucket usage-events-store and the IAM role LedgerlineReporterRole are both in account 888800002222. Access is provided only by the role's identity-based policy. Attach a policy that allows storage:ListBucket on usage-events-store for the prefix events/daily/. Allow storage:GetObject on usage-events-store/events/daily/*. Allow storage:PutObject on usage-events-store/exports/* so each report run can write its files. Keep the bucket policy as it is, with no added statements. Trigger a manual run and check that exports/ contains one PDF and one CSV for the reporting date.

This guide configures a scheduled report generator, Ledgerline, which reads daily event tables and writes PDF and CSV report exports. The bucket usage-events-store belongs to account 999900003333, and the IAM role LedgerlineReporterRole belongs to account 888800002222. Access is granted by the bucket owner through the bucket policy. Add a statement in account 999900003333 that names arn:iam::888800002222:role/LedgerlineReporterRole as the principal. Allow storage:ListBucket on usage-events-store for the prefix events/daily/. Allow storage:GetObject on usage-events-store/events/daily/*. Allow storage:PutObject on usage-events-store/exports/* so each report run can write its files. The role's account must also allow these actions in the role's policy. Trigger a manual run and check that exports/ contains one PDF and one CSV for the reporting date.

This guide describes access for Schemascout, a catalog crawler that reads sample objects to infer schemas and writes manifest files describing each table. The bucket datalake-raw-zone and the IAM role SchemascoutCrawlerRole are in account 333344445555. The role's identity-based policy is the only source of the grant. Allow storage:ListBucket on datalake-raw-zone without a prefix restriction so the crawler can enumerate table folders. Allow storage:GetObject on datalake-raw-zone/tables/* for sampling the first objects of each table. Allow storage:PutObject on datalake-raw-zone/_manifests/* for the generated schema manifests. No bucket policy change is made. After a crawl, open a manifest in _manifests/ and confirm that column names and types match the source files.

This guide describes access for Schemascout, a catalog crawler that reads sample objects to infer schemas and writes manifest files describing each table. The bucket datalake-raw-zone is owned by account 101010202020, and the IAM role SchemascoutCrawlerRole is in account 333344445555. The bucket owner provides the grant in a bucket policy statement. In account 101010202020, add a statement with the principal arn:iam::333344445555:role/SchemascoutCrawlerRole. Allow storage:ListBucket on datalake-raw-zone without a prefix restriction so the crawler can enumerate table folders. Allow storage:GetObject on datalake-raw-zone/tables/* for sampling and storage:PutObject on datalake-raw-zone/_manifests/*. The role's account must also allow these actions in the role's policy. After a crawl, open a manifest in _manifests/ and confirm that column names and types match the source files.

This guide sets up a feature pipeline, Vectorbench, that reads clickstream files and writes feature snapshot files for model training. The bucket clickstream-curated and the IAM role VectorbenchPipelineRole both exist in account 404040505050. The pipeline's permissions are defined solely in the role's identity-based policy. Allow storage:ListBucket on clickstream-curated for the prefixes sessions/ and snapshots/. Allow storage:GetObject on clickstream-curated/sessions/*. Allow storage:PutObject and storage:AbortMultipartUpload on clickstream-curated/snapshots/*, since snapshots are large and uploaded in parts. Do not alter the bucket policy. Run the pipeline for one day of data and confirm that a completed snapshot object exists under snapshots/ with no incomplete multipart uploads left.

This guide sets up a feature pipeline, Vectorbench, that reads clickstream files and writes feature snapshot files for model training. The bucket clickstream-curated is owned by account 606060707070, and the IAM role VectorbenchPipelineRole is in account 404040505050. The bucket owner grants access with a bucket policy statement. In account 606060707070, add a statement naming arn:iam::404040505050:role/VectorbenchPipelineRole as the principal. Allow storage:ListBucket on clickstream-curated for the prefixes sessions/ and snapshots/. Allow storage:GetObject on clickstream-curated/sessions/*, and storage:PutObject and storage:AbortMultipartUpload on clickstream-curated/snapshots/* because snapshots are uploaded in parts. The role's account must also permit these actions in the role's policy. Run the pipeline for one day of data and confirm that a completed snapshot object exists under snapshots/ with no incomplete multipart uploads left.

This guide gives an analyst user, working in the Quarrywise notebook service, access to read datasets and write query results. The bucket finance-datasets and the IAM user analyst-mkim are in account 121212343434. The grant is made in an identity-based policy attached to analyst-mkim, or to a group the user belongs to. Allow storage:ListBucket on finance-datasets for the prefix curated/. Allow storage:GetObject on finance-datasets/curated/*. Allow storage:PutObject on finance-datasets/scratch/analyst-mkim/* so query results are written to a personal location. The bucket policy is not changed. Run a notebook query and confirm that the result file is created under scratch/analyst-mkim/ and that writes elsewhere in the bucket are denied.

This guide gives an analyst user, working in the Quarrywise notebook service, access to read datasets and write query results. The bucket finance-datasets is owned by account 565656787878, and the IAM user analyst-mkim is in account 121212343434. The bucket owner makes the grant with a bucket policy statement. In account 565656787878, add a statement naming arn:iam::121212343434:user/analyst-mkim as the principal. Allow storage:ListBucket on finance-datasets for the prefix curated/. Allow storage:GetObject on finance-datasets/curated/*. Allow storage:PutObject on finance-datasets/scratch/analyst-mkim/* so query results are written to a personal location. The user's account must also permit these actions in the user's policy. Runa notebook query and confirm that the result file is created under scratch/analyst-mkim/ and that writes elsewhere in the bucket are denied.

This guide configures Dedupbay, a deduplication job that reads landing-zone files and writes unique records to a curated zone. The bucket ingest-lake and the IAM role DedupbayWorkerRole are in account 747474858585. Access comes only from the role's identity-based policy. Allow storage:ListBucket on ingest-lake for the prefixes landing/ and curated/. Allow storage:GetObject on ingest-lake/landing/* and storage:PutObject on ingest-lake/curated/*. Add a policy condition requiring that uploads specify server-side encryption, matching the bucket's default setting. Leave the bucket policy unmodified. Run the job on a test file that contains duplicate rows and confirm that the object in curated/ has each record only once.

This guide configures Dedupbay, a deduplication job that reads landing-zone files and writes unique records to a curated zone. The bucket ingest-lake is owned by account 959595060606, and the IAM role DedupbayWorkerRole is in account 747474858585. The bucket owner grants access by adding a bucket policy statement. In account 959595060606, name arn:iam::747474858585:role/DedupbayWorkerRole as the principal. Allow storage:ListBucket on ingest-lake for the prefixes landing/ and curated/. Allow storage:GetObject on ingest-lake/landing/* and storage:PutObject on ingest-lake/curated/*, with a condition requiring that uploads specify server-side encryption. The role's account must also allow these actions in the role's policy. Run the job on a test file that contains duplicate rows and confirm that the object in curated/ has each record only once.
